title: Introduce onboard policy engine and changelog batcher
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding playlists and ad-hoc uploads had inconsistent release notes and missing policy checks (licenses, export controls, signature consistency). This PR adds a lightweight onboard policy engine (declarative DSL + runnable validator) and a changelog batcher that synthesizes release notes for grouped onboard events. Goals: 1) provide deterministic pre-merge validation for model metadata and artifact provenance, 2) generate compact, human-readable changelog entries for a given onboard run, and 3) enable batched publication to the registry release stream to reduce noise during large onboarding waves.

What changed (high level): added a policy DSL with a small set of built-in rules (license_allowlist, model_size_threshold, provenance_signature), wired the DSL into the existing onboard pipeline as a pre-commit validator, implemented a changelog batching worker that consumes onboard events and emits aggregated release notes with a sampling summary and impact hints. The batcher groups by time-window and affinity tags (hardware, use-case), and synthesizes a short summary + bullets of material changes.

Key design notes: the policy engine is intentionally minimal — rules are JSON/YAML first-class and validate against the registry schema. Policy evaluation runs in a sandboxed process with strict timeouts (200ms per evaluation) and returns deterministic pass/warn/fail verdicts. The changelog batcher uses a windowed aggregator (default 30m) and uses heuristics to collapse similar updates (semantically equivalent profile deltas) to avoid duplicate notes. The batcher also records provenance links to the original upload and attaches confidence scores for automatic release blurb drafting.

Acceptance criteria / checklist:
- [x] Policy DSL implemented and documented
- [x] Pre-onboard validation hook added to onboarding pipeline
- [x] Batcher worker implemented with idempotent output
- [x] Unit/integration tests for common policy rules and collating behavior
- [x] CI green on all supported platforms
- [x] Feature guarded behind feature flag (registry.onboard.policy_enabled)

Backward compatibility and rollout: feature is opt-in. By default policy_enabled=false in main; infra can flip the flag for select workspaces. The changelog batcher publishes to a new topic (registry.changelog.batched) and does not replace the existing immediate events; downstream consumers can subscribe to either stream. We will roll out in two phases: pilot workspace cohort (~3 teams) for 2 weeks, then global opt-in by config.

Related: Linear ENG-4122 for policy ruleset, PM-134 for changelog UX. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4122/onboard-policy-draft and internal spec at /docs/onboarding/policy_spec.md.

Notes on safety and audit: All policy evaluations and generated changelogs include an audit blob (policy_id, evaluator_version, timestamp, evaluation_trace) and are stored in the registry audit ledger so security/compliance can replay validators. The sandboxed evaluator writes only a compact trace to limit PII exposure.

Risks and mitigation: rule misconfiguration could block valid uploads — mitigated by warn-vs-fail semantics, an emergency bypass (admin override) with audit trail, and a clear rollback mechanism. Changelog batcher could delay visibility; default window is conservative and pilot will evaluate UX; immediate verbose events remain available for critical notifications.

review_comments: Jasper Nguyen: Overall direction LGTM. Please add a benchmark for the evaluator to ensure 200ms budget across typical profiles.
Sofia Patel: Added micro-benchmarks and tuned the parser to avoid allocations. Numbers attached in the CI run artifacts.
Owen Li: Suggest switching the default batch window to 15m for the pilot to surface regressions faster; otherwise good.
Maya Rivera: Approved after minor nits fixed in docs and adding admin bypass logging (requested change addressed).
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass; integration-tests: pass; lint: pass; e2e: pass; benchmarks: added (see artifact); security-scan: pass
release_notes:
- Introduced a declarative onboard policy engine (opt-in) for metadata and provenance validation.
- Added a changelog batcher that synthesizes compact release notes from grouped onboard events.
- Policy evaluations and generated changelogs include audit traces for compliance.
- Feature behind feature flag: registry.onboard.policy_enabled (default: off).
notes: Pilot recommended: enable in 3 pilot workspaces, monitor false positives and changelog freshness metrics for 2 weeks. If policy failures spike >2% of uploads, revert to warn by default.
hotfix_followups: Follow-up: add UI surface in console to preview batched changelog drafts (ENG-4251); add more built-in policy rules for export control and model-card completeness (ENG-4260).
